title: Component preimages from finite closed descent under a surjection
statement: Let p:Y -> Z be a continuous surjection of topological spaces. Suppose Y has finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components], and each component C is the full inverse image of some closed subset of Z. Then for every irreducible component A of Z, p^{-1}(A) is an irreducible component of Y.

source.place: isIrreducible_iff_sUnion_isClosed, IsIrreducible.image; finite descent conclusion in Tag 054R. Topological proof written by the second reader.

proof.text: The images p(C) of upstairs components form a finite closed cover of Z. Surjectivity shows p(p^{-1}(D))=D for each descended subset D, so each image is closed. The component cover of Y and surjectivity imply these images cover Z.

For a component A of Z, the finite closed-cover criterion isIrreducible_iff_sUnion_isClosed gives A contained in p(C) for some component C of Y. Continuous images of irreducible sets are irreducible, so maximality of A gives A=p(C). The descent equality for C and surjectivity give p^{-1}(p(C))=C. Thus p^{-1}(A)=C, as required. For empty Z there is no A.
